bib.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning", Alayrac, Donahue, Luc, Miech, ... Zisserman, Simonyan (DeepMind). NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv:2204.14198v2, 15 Nov 2022). File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/08-multimodal-engineering/sources/alayrac-2022-flamingo.pdf

COVERAGE: I read 190,811 characters out of 190,811 across 54 pages. I read 0–40,000 and 77,000–190,811 in full: the main text, the checklist, and Appendices A–G, including the model card and datasheets. I only skimmed the references (about 40,000–77,091), plus targeted lookups for the BUILDS ON list.

AUDIT OF THE NOTE'S NUMBERS
1. 64 visual tokens from the Perceiver Resampler: confirmed. "produces a fixed number of visual outputs (64)" (§2.1, p.5). The resampler is the same about 200M-parameter (194M in Table 5) "Medium" size, with 6 layers, in all three model sizes.
2. Frozen 70B Chinchilla: confirmed. Flamingo-80B = 70B frozen LM + 435M frozen NFNet-F6 + 10B trainable GATED XATTN-DENSE (inserted every 7th layer) + 194M resampler (Table 5, p.28).
3. tanh gates initialised at zero: confirmed. "α is a layer-specific learnable scalar initialized to 0" (p.5). In the 3B ablation, removing them costs 4.2 points of Overall score and causes "training instabilities" (p.9).
4. "32-shot beats fine-tuned SOTA on 6 of 16 benchmarks": confirmed, but tighten the setup. The 6 are among 15 comparable tasks, because RareAct has no fine-tuned result. From Table 1 they are OKVQA, MSVDQA, Flickr30K, iVQA, STAR and NextQA. The Table 1 caption itself says "on seven tasks", which contradicts the text and Fig. 2 ("6 of the 16"). Use 6.
5. VQAv2 67.6% vs 80.2%: confirmed with setup. Both are VQAv2 test-dev, VQA accuracy, Flamingo-80B, 32 shots. 80.2 is Florence [140], fine-tuned on 444K examples (Table 1). Caveats:
   - (a) The unrestricted SotA, which uses ensembling, is 81.3 (Yan et al. [133], Table 2/8).
   - (b) Fine-tuned Flamingo reaches 82.0 test-dev and 82.1 test-std.
   - (c) Appendix B.2.2 gives the 32-shot figure as "67.3%", which is inconsistent with the 67.6 in the tables.
   - (d) VQAv2 is a DEV benchmark, which the authors say "may be biased, as a result of model selection".
6. 3B ablations, 8.0% and 12.9%: the numbers are right, but the units need care. The metric is the "Overall score": each benchmark score is divided by its Table 1 SotA, then averaged over the 5 DEV benchmarks (validation subsets, 4 shots, short schedule). The baseline is 70.7. Fine-tuning the pretrained LM gives 62.7, a drop of 8.0 points. Training the LM from random init gives 57.8, a drop of 12.9 points. These are absolute drops in a percent-of-SotA average, not relative percentage drops. Fine-tuning the LM also raises step time from 1.74s to 2.42s. The paper frames the 8.0 drop as catastrophic forgetting.

  where: p.9, Table 3 row (viii)
- claim: The interleaved web data (M3W) matters most in the data mix; image-text pairs matter too.

  setup: same 3B ablation
  quote: "removing the interleaved image-text dataset M3W leads to a decrease of more than 17% in performance while removing the conventional paired image-text pairs also decreases performance (by 9.8%)"

LIMITS:
- Hallucinations and ungrounded guesses are attributed to the LM priors (Fig. 13).
- The model inherits the LM's poor length generalisation and its causal-only conditioning.
- Classification trails contrastive models.
- In-context learning is sensitive to example order and format.
- Inference cost scales linearly with shots if the KV cache is reused, and quadratically otherwise.
- Performance "plateaus rapidly as the number of few-shot samples increases beyond 32".
- Text is an awkward interface for boxes, dense prediction or continuous outputs.
- There are no error bars: each model was trained once.
- The DEV benchmarks (COCO, OKVQA, VQAv2, MSVDQA, VATEX) are biased by model selection. Only 11 benchmarks are held out.
- The model is English-only. Code and data are proprietary and not released.
- VizWiz, HatefulMemes and TextVQA were not deduplicated against training data, and M3W was not deduplicated: 1314 near-duplicate candidates, of which 125 are exact duplicates.
- Only sexually explicit content was filtered; toxic content was not.
- The bias study is preliminary: COCO captioning showed no significant gender or skin-tone CIDEr gap, lowest p = 0.25. Intersectional bias was not studied.
- The model card says research use only.
- Dated: these are 2022 SotA comparisons, and the NFNet encoder and Chinchilla LM are not public.

BUILDS ON: Perceiver (Jaegle et al. 2021 [48]); DETR (Carion et al. 2020 [13]); tanh gating from LSTM (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber 1997 [41]); zero-init residual from ReZero (Bachlechner et al. 2021 [4]); Chinchilla (Hoffmann et al. 2022 [42]); NFNet (Brock et al. 2021 [10]); CLIP contrastive loss (Radford et al. [85]); ALIGN dataset (Jia et al. [50]); Frozen (Tsimpoukelli et al. 2021 [114]); GPT-3 in-context learning (Brown et al. 2020 [11]); RICES (Yang et al. 2021 [136]); the compared alternatives VirTex (Desai & Johnson 2021 [22]) and VC-GPT "grafting" (Luo et al. 2022 [68]); Megatron (Shoeybi et al. [99]); ZeRO [88].

CODE:
- p.5, Fig. 4:
  y = y + tanh(alpha_xattn) * attention(q=y, kv=x)
  y = y + tanh(alpha_dense) * ffw(y)
  y = y + frozen_attention(q=y, kv=y)
  y = y + frozen_ffw(y)
- p.23, Fig. 5 (Perceiver Resampler):
  x_f = x_f + time_embeddings
  x_f = flatten(x_f)  # [T, S, d] -> [T * S, d]
  for i in range(num_layers):
    x = x + attention_i(q=x, kv=concat([x_f, x]))
    x = x + ffw_i(x)
  Note that the keys and values concatenate the latents with the visual features. The resampler uses no spatial position encodings, only temporal ones.

FIGURES:
- Fig. 3 (p.4), architecture overview: the frozen and trained parts in one picture.
- Fig. 4 (p.5), GATED XATTN-DENSE with pseudo-code: shows the zero-init gate at a glance.
- Fig. 5 (p.23), Perceiver Resampler: a variable-size grid goes in and a fixed set of tokens comes out.
- Fig. 7 (p.24), per-image cross-attention masking on interleaved text: makes the "attend to the last image only" rule concrete.
- Fig. 6 (p.24), gate magnitudes growing from 0 during training.
- Fig. 13 (p.42), hallucination and ungrounded-guess examples: a ready-made failure-mode illustration.

PROBLEMS:
- Page 42 contains an embedded fragment of a different draft of Appendix D.1. It cites "Section 4.2" and author-year references, and claims "a large drop of roughly 30% in relative performance on VisDial when going from 16-shots to 32-shot". That claim does not appear in the main v2 text, so I would not cite it without checking the rendered page.
- Internal inconsistencies: "six" vs "seven" tasks (Table 1 caption), and 67.6 vs 67.3 for VQAv2 32-shot (B.2.2).
- Table cells in the extraction are run together, so I recomputed the ablation deltas from the Table 3 rows: 70.7 → 62.7 / 57.8 / 66.5 / 53.4 / 60.9.
- The PDF contains no embedded instructions.
